strategy.thesis: Investment arm of the Business Development Bank of Canada (a federal Crown corporation). Runs thematic funds (Deep Tech, Climate Tech, Seed, Life Sciences, Sustainability, Women in Technology/Thrive).

summary.en: BDC Capital is the investment arm of the Business Development Bank of Canada, a wholly government-owned federal Crown corporation. It is described as Canada's largest and most active venture capital investor, operating both as a direct investor across stages and as the country's most active limited partner in independent VC funds, with thematic funds spanning deep tech, climate, life sciences and women in tech.

aka: Venture and Growth Capital Catalyst Initiative

funds.name: Venture and Growth Capital Catalyst Initiative (Growth VCCI)

strategy.thesis: Federal fund-of-funds program designed to increase the supply of venture capital for high-potential Canadian firms by investing in funds-of-funds and VC funds (with dedicated life sciences and inclusive-growth/emerging-manager streams), administered by BDC on behalf of the Government of Canada.

summary.en: VCCI is a Government of Canada venture capital program that invests in funds-of-funds and VC funds to leverage private capital into Canada's startup ecosystem. It began as VCCI 2017 ($371M), was renewed in Budget 2021 ($450M across funds-of-funds, life sciences and inclusive-growth streams), and Budget 2025 announced a successor $1B Venture and Growth Capital Catalyst Initiative. It is managed by BDC on behalf of the federal government.

summary.en: Futurpreneur Canada is a national non-profit (federally funded, with BDC and corporate partners) that provides collateral-free startup loans of up to $75,000 plus up to two years of mentorship to young entrepreneurs aged 18-39, including dedicated streams for Black, Indigenous and newcomer founders. It has supported 21,000+ entrepreneurs and provided $259 million in startup loans since 1996.

summary.en: NRC IRAP is the National Research Council of Canada's flagship innovation-assistance program, providing non-repayable grants plus advisory support and connections to Canadian SMEs conducting technology R&D. Funding typically ranges from tens of thousands to $500,000 (up to $10M for major projects), covering up to 80% of internal technical labour. It is a leading early-stage funding source for Canadian startups, distributing on the order of $400M+ annually.

summary.en: SDTC was an arm's-length foundation created by the Government of Canada in 2001 to fund clean-technology development and demonstration by Canadian companies, investing over $1.15 billion across roughly 400 companies. Following governance issues, it was disbanded as an independent foundation on 4 June 2024 and its programming was folded into the National Research Council Canada.

strategy.thesis: Large federal contribution program supporting transformative, large-scale R&D, commercialization and expansion projects (typically $10M+ contributions for projects of $20M+); aimed at major firms and innovation networks rather than small startups. Closed to new applications and succeeded by the Strategic Response Fund.

summary.en: The Strategic Innovation Fund is a federal ISED contribution program launched in 2017 that funds large-scale innovation, R&D commercialization and industrial expansion projects, with contributions generally starting at $10M for projects of at least $20M in eligible costs. It has deployed $9.2B across 127 projects plus $1.2B across 16 networks, and is now closed to new applications, succeeded by the Strategic Response Fund.

summary.en: Innovative Solutions Canada is a federal procurement and grant program (modelled on the US SBIR) in which ~20 participating federal departments set aside roughly 1% of budgets to fund and buy early-stage innovations from Canadian SMEs. It offers Phase 1 proof-of-concept grants up to $150,000 and Phase 2 prototype grants up to $1 million, awarding about $79.7M across 131 grants/contracts in 2022-23. The program has been scaled back under federal spending review.

It received $284 million from the Government of Canada (plus Quebec provincial and private matching) and co-invests with industry on a matched basis.

summary.en: Mitacs is a national not-for-profit research organization, jointly funded by the federal and provincial governments and partners, that connects companies (including startups) with university and college researchers via co-funded internship and R&D programs such as Accelerate and Globalink. It is a major talent-and-innovation funding bridge for Canadian startups, and received an $800M federal commitment to expand its programs.

It is a loan-access program, not an equity investor.

summary.en: Alberta Enterprise Corporation is a provincial Crown corporation formed by the Government of Alberta in 2008 to build a local venture capital industry. It invests indirectly as a limited partner in VC funds with an Alberta presence, having committed C$415 million across 39 funds as of December 2024.
